newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian parliament agrees child sex scandal report.
newsitem.headline: Belgian parliament agrees child sex scandal report.

text.p: The Belgian parliament, despite some clear differences of opinion, on Friday approved unanimously a scathing report into bungled investigations into the country's child abuse and murder scandal.
"The motion is carried unanimously," Parliament President Raymond Langendries told the packed lower house.
The vote by the 137 deputies followed two days of debate that exposed tensions between the Francophone Liberal opposition party and the four parties in the centre-left coalition.

But in the end, and in the knowledge that public opinion would slaughter them if they let party politics stand in the way of the report by the special parliamentary commission, they buried their differences and voted together.

The report, which follows six months of often televised hearings that gripped and disgusted the nation, spares no-one in its description of the shambolic investigations into the spate of child kidnappings, rapes and murders that came to light last August. So far the bodies of five young girls have been found.

The report also makes a series of recommendations ranging from creation of a single police force to replace the existing three rival forces, to giving parents of missing children greater access to the investigations and reform of the whole justice system.
